`stock_report.py` now flags an item as `REORDER` when what's on hand won't cover the 6 days an order takes to arrive. I ran it against your current `inventory.csv`:

```
SKU      ITEM                       ON HAND  STATUS
CF-1K    House blend 1kg                  9  REORDER
CF-250   Colombia beans 250g             42  ok
FL-100   Paper filters x100               0  OUT
MG-12    Enamel mug                      18  ok
OT-1L    Oat milk 1L                     30  REORDER
TE-50    Breakfast tea x50               25  ok
```

- **The setting:** `LEAD_TIME_DAYS = 6` sits just under the imports at the top of the file; change that one number if you switch suppliers.
- **The rule:** an item is flagged when on-hand is at or below average daily sales × 6. House blend sells 2.4 a day, so it needs 14.4 to last and has 9; oat milk needs 45 and has 30.
- **Exactly enough counts as flagged:** if stock would run out on the very day the delivery lands, it shows `REORDER`, because waiting for the next night's report would leave the shelf empty for a day.
- **`OUT` is unchanged:** an empty shelf still shows `OUT` rather than `REORDER`, so you can tell the two apart.

The report doesn't know whether you've already placed an order, so an item keeps showing `REORDER` each night until the stock actually arrives.
